entities.summary:
Albert Daeger (1872–1932) was an American Franciscan missionary bishop who served as Archbishop of Santa Fe in New Mexico, leading one of the oldest and most historically complex Catholic archdioceses in the United States. A Franciscan friar from Ohio, he was appointed Archbishop of Santa Fe in 1919 and led the archdiocese until his death in 1932.

Santa Fe's archdiocese was extraordinary in American Catholic terms: it encompassed the oldest Catholic communities in what is now the United States, rooted in the Spanish Franciscan missions of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, and included large Native American Catholic populations (primarily Pueblo peoples), Hispanic Catholic communities maintaining centuries-old traditions, and a growing Anglo-American Catholic immigrant population. Managing this ethnic and cultural diversity was the central challenge of the archiepiscopate.

Daeger engaged the challenges of Native American Catholic communities, the relationship between the archdiocese and the Pueblo communities' traditional religious practices, and the development of educational and social institutions in one of the most economically underdeveloped areas of the United States. His Franciscan background—rooted in the order that had conducted the original sixteenth-century mission in New Mexico—gave him a special connection to the archdiocese's deep historical roots.
